prompt:
Style: european-travel-film. Transform the supplied ORIGINAL photograph of a LEGO Millennium Falcon model on a white cabinet, minifigures, a display plaque and nearby autumn foliage. Render only a single full-frame artwork using this style treatment:

- **artwork — grading only, no re-rendering.** The same photograph, viewpoint, framing and scene as the foundation, re-graded with a Dazz analog-film feel and Lightroom-style colour grading toward a European vintage travel-editorial look. Grading adapts per photo: gently reduce excessive saturation; muted steel-blue/gray-blue skies where appropriate; authentic stone, brick, wood and metal colours preserved; greenery subdued without losing detail; realistic water reflections, warm sunset tones, natural skin colours and recognisable colours of vibrant subjects retained; no single orange-brown, golden or blue palette imposed on all images. Highlights and shadows refined with gentle cinematic contrast, detail and dimensionality retained, overly digital sharpness softened, subtle realistic fine film grain added. No exaggerated light leaks, scratches, timestamps, heavy filters, artificial colour casts or excessive vintage effects. All buildings, structures, people, animals, terrain, roads, waterways, sky composition, object counts, scales, positions, perspective and meaningful details are preserved in both halves; no invented clouds, weather changes, new light sources, replaced backgrounds or reconstructed scenery. - **Final check.** Strict equal 50/50 split, original on top, composition and subjects as consistent as possible, naturally graded vintage-film travel-editorial interpretation below, one refined poster per input photo. 

Preserve the original scene's subject relationships. Every part of the canvas must belong to the transformed artwork. No original photo panel, no before/after comparison, no split, no text.
